section_summary: This section covers proposals for Japanese Antarctic whaling in 1949–50 and disputes over expanding Japan’s authorized fishing area. It includes SCAP memoranda, diplomatic despatches, industry representatives’ views, and Far Eastern Commission policy papers on conservation, consultation, and reparations. The final pages begin a Natural Resources Section weekly summary covering fisheries and agricultural matters.

subfiles.title: Recommendation for a third Japanese Antarctic whaling fleet
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Recommends a three-factory-ship Japanese Antarctic expedition for 1949–50.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that a third fleet would increase food and oil production and reduce United States costs. It answers anticipated objections about competition, Japan’s prewar conduct, and SCAP authority, then recommends notifying the Department of the Army.

subfiles.title: Tab A: Japanese Antarctic Whaling Production
subfiles.about: Compares past catches and projected 1949–50 production and savings.
subfiles.summary: Projects 1,500 blue whale units and $22 million in savings for three fleets.

subfiles.title: Tab B: Nations Participating in Antarctic Whaling, 1948–1949 Season
subfiles.about: Lists participating countries, factory ships, and shore stations.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Antarctic whaling fleets and shore stations for the 1948–49 season.

subfiles.title: Tab C: Availability of Shipping for Third Antarctic Whaling Fleet
subfiles.about: Reports that sufficient vessels are available for a third Japanese fleet.
subfiles.summary: SCAJAP officers reported available tankers and catcher boats and raised no objection to their diversion.

subfiles.title: Tab D: Objection of Norway and Britain to Japanese Participation in Antarctic Whaling
subfiles.about: Responds to Norwegian and British objections to Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: Terry argues that the catch limit protects whale stocks rather than national market shares. He invokes the Atlantic Charter and Potsdam Declaration and estimates that a third fleet would add oil and food for Japan.

subfiles.title: Tab E: Japanese Violations of International Whaling Regulations
subfiles.about: Assesses compliance and efficiency of postwar Japanese whaling expeditions.
subfiles.summary: Terry contrasts prewar violations with low reported illegal catches under SCAP supervision in 1946–49. He also cites improved oil yield per blue whale unit and concludes that Japanese operations compare favorably with other nations.

subfiles.title: Tab F: Australian Government’s Question of SCAP Authority Authorizing Whaling
subfiles.about: Reviews Australia’s challenge and the United States response on SCAP whaling authority.
subfiles.summary: Cites a 1948 State Department radio affirming SCAP’s authority to authorize and size an expedition.

subfiles.title: Tab G: Proposed message on 1949–50 Antarctic whaling
subfiles.doc_type: draft outgoing message with note for record
subfiles.to: Department of the Army; Department of State
subfiles.about: Drafts notice of a three-fleet expedition under SCAP supervision.
subfiles.summary: The draft proposes three factory ships, estimates 17,000 additional metric tons of products and about $4 million in savings, and promises compliance monitoring. Its note explains the authority and rationale.

subfiles.title: Views of United States Fishing Representatives toward Expansion of the Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a conversation memorandum on United States fishing representatives’ views.
subfiles.summary: Reports concern about Japanese fishing near the Trust Territory, Bering Sea, and Alaska.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fishing Operations
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Records visiting fishing representatives’ discussion with SCAP and mission officers.
subfiles.summary: The participants discuss procedures for expanding Japan’s fishing area, objections to operations in the Trust Territory and Pacific Northwest, and fears about conservation practices. They also consider patrols and possible peace treaty provisions governing Japanese fishing.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram concerning Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Discusses a request concerning Japanese whaling; much of the OCR is unreadable.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text refers to the Natural Resources Section and Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Expansion of Japanese Fishing Area
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports conditions and diplomatic concerns affecting expansion of Japan’s fishing area.
subfiles.summary: The mission says SCAP expects Japanese compliance, a patrol or inspection system, and stronger conservation before considering expansion. It notes unanswered Philippine views on waters near Luzon and a proposed fleet reduction, while cautioning against indefinite delay.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fishermen Warned of Invading American Areas
subfiles.about: Reports American experts’ warning about Japanese fishing near North America.
subfiles.summary: The experts call for observance and patrol of the MacArthur line before expansion.

subfiles.title: Proposed Fishing Area Extension Near Luzon
subfiles.about: Requests Philippine views on a proposed Japanese fishing area extension.
subfiles.summary: Describes the proposed boundary near Luzon and asks the Philippine Mission to obtain its government’s views.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph on Whaling
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards five copies of a Japanese Foreign Office whaling monograph.
subfiles.summary: Describes the monograph’s account of whaling’s economic value and Japan’s wish to continue Antarctic operations.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Territorial Sovereignty over Formosa and the Kurile Islands
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Clarifies that final territorial sovereignty awaits a peace settlement.
subfiles.summary: Advises avoiding public views while privately considering Japanese claims to four northern island groups.

subfiles.title: Army Comments on Fishing and Aquatic Industries in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes amendments to the Far Eastern Commission fisheries policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Porter asks for explicit conservation language, a narrower consent requirement when expanding fishing areas, and deletion of a reparations paragraph that the Army fears would discourage Japanese investors.

subfiles.title: United States Understanding of Direct Concern in Fishing Areas
subfiles.about: Explains how member states’ direct concern over fishing areas should be assessed.
subfiles.summary: The statement accepts reasonable security and conservation claims but says SCAP may exercise discretion against excessive claims, subject to Far Eastern Commission review.

subfiles.title: Reply to Colonel Porter on Fisheries Policy Amendments
subfiles.about: Responds to Army proposals for the fisheries policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Bishop accepts conservation wording and seeks deletion of the reparations paragraph. He resists reopening the direct-concern provision after other delegations accepted the United States interpretation.

subfiles.title: Instructions on Fishing and Aquatic Industries in Japan
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Instructs the delegate to seek deletion of paragraph 5.
subfiles.summary: If deletion fails, the draft calls for a statement protecting the United States reparations position.

subfiles.title: Duplicate concluding page of Bishop’s draft reply
subfiles.about: Repeats the conclusion of the draft reply on fisheries policy amendments.
subfiles.summary: Reiterates the plan to seek deletion of paragraph 5 and consult the Army.

subfiles.title: Discussion with Mr. West on FEC Japanese Fishing Paper
subfiles.about: Records agreement to consult SCAP and insist on deleting the reparations paragraph.
subfiles.summary: Bishop proposes asking SCAP about paragraph 2b and threatening a veto if paragraph 5 remains.

subfiles.title: United States Position on FEC Paper, Fishing and Aquatic Industries in Japan
subfiles.about: Explains the proposed United States response to Army objections to the fisheries paper.
subfiles.summary: Bishop reviews earlier negotiations over fishing-area consent and the Army’s later amendment requests. He recommends accepting conservation wording and seeking removal of paragraph 5, while initially opposing a veto if that deletion fails.

subfiles.title: SC-271/19: Fishing and Aquatic Industries in Japan
subfiles.doc_type: Far Eastern Commission circulation note and proposed policy
subfiles.about: Circulates amended proposed policy on Japanese fishing and aquatic industries.
subfiles.summary: The policy sets a proposed fishing-area boundary, permits expansion subject to security and consultation, requires vessel identification and conservation practices, and retains a contested reparations clause. The circulation note identifies an outstanding United States amendment to paragraph 2b.

subfiles.title: Authorization of 1949–1950 Japanese Antarctic Whaling Expedition
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP’s proposed formal authorization for a two-fleet expedition.
subfiles.summary: Reports that early authorization would allow Japanese preparations for the coming season.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section Request for Whaling Directive
subfiles.about: Urges prompt issuance of a Japanese Antarctic whaling directive.
subfiles.summary: Cites necessary ship repairs and financing that depend on official authorization.

subfiles.title: Proposed SCAP Directive on Japanese Whaling Operations, with Note for Record
subfiles.about: Sets conditions for a two-fleet Antarctic expedition in 1949–50.
subfiles.summary: The draft requires approval of vessels and managers, route and position reporting, catch records, inspectors, fuel accounting, vessel surveys, and cargo verification. It disclaims precedent for later seasons or territorial claims. An attached note explains the decision to authorize two fleets after an earlier three-fleet proposal.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Natural Resources Section Request for Whaling Directive
subfiles.about: Duplicates the request to issue the whaling directive promptly.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the need for authorization to secure repairs and financing.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Proposed SCAP Directive on Japanese Whaling Operations
subfiles.about: Duplicates the proposed two-fleet authorization and operating conditions.
subfiles.summary: The repeated draft sets approval, inspection, reporting, survey, and cargo requirements for the 1949–50 expedition. Its note again records the decision to proceed with two fleets.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram on Paragraph 6 of the FEC Fisheries Paper
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Urges deletion of a contested paragraph in the fisheries policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo argues that foreign enforcement claims could undermine SCAP’s control of Japan’s fishing-area rules.

subfiles.title: Reply on Deletion of Paragraph 6
subfiles.about: Reports that the committee has agreed to delete paragraph 6.
subfiles.summary: Confirms deletion of the disputed paragraph from the FEC fisheries paper.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese Fishing Industry Prepared by Visiting American Experts
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards the visiting experts’ report in Natural Resources Section Weekly Summary No. 189.
subfiles.summary: Huston says the experts endorse SCAP fisheries controls, a Japanese patrol, stronger administration, and eventual fishery treaties. They oppose Japanese coastal fishing off Allied powers and support the resumption of whaling.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Despatch No. 395 on Visiting American Experts
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the cover despatch forwarding the experts’ fisheries report.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the experts’ endorsement of SCAP controls, patrols, and fishery treaties.

subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section Weekly Summary No. 189
subfiles.about: Begins the weekly summary for 22–28 May 1949.
subfiles.summary: The cover and contents list agricultural, fisheries, forestry, mining, and petroleum reports, including the visiting experts’ fisheries review later in the issue. The reproduced opening pages report cooperative liquidation, staple-crop collections, milk production, fertilizer distribution, fish-meal controls, and agricultural research reform. The weekly summary continues beyond page 538.
